messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 tail latency spike detected for /v1/stream (SSE + websocket) — thresholds breached at 22:09 UTC. Multiple customers seeing stalls and partial chunk delivery.

maya: seeing the same in dashboard — p95 ~ 450ms, p99 jumped to 6.2s, a lot of requests stuck in PROXY_WRITE.

rene: logs show repeated ECONNRESETs from our stream-proxy to backend workers around the spike window. Could be client backpressure piling up at the proxy.

zara: confirmed customer-reported behavior: partial chunks, then long silence, then final chunk. Browser clients report socket stays open.

maya: initial quick triage: is this limited to a region or all regions?

ops-bot: region filter: eu-west-1 and us-east-1 both show anomalies. Cross-region blue/green suggests routing fallback triggered for some traffic.

tom: grabbing proxy metrics: write queue length on stream-proxy nodes increased by ~3-5x. TCP retransmits also up. Possibly slow consumers causing head-of-line blocking in the proxy.

rene: can we temporarily increase keepalive and proxy write timeout to mitigate? If clients are slow, we may need to flush and close slow connections to protect tails.

maya: proposing mitigation steps: 1) increase proxy chunk-write timeout from 10s -> 20s; 2) enable per-connection chunk-rate limiting (soft limit) to avoid large slowdown; 3) patch upstream to drop stalled connections after X bytes queued. Will push a canary to 10% of traffic. Thoughts?

zara: +1 for canary. Need to notify customers if we drop connections. Which metric will we watch to roll back? p99 and proxy write queue length.

rene: command to toggle timeout via config service: ```
# update via cfgctl
cfgctl set stream-proxy.write_timeout 20s --env prod --canary 0.1
cfgctl set stream-proxy.per_conn_rate_limit 64kbps --env prod --canary 0.1
```

maya: rolling canary now. Triggered at 22:14 UTC. Will post progress every 2 min.

ops-bot: Incident NOTE: customer impact = degraded streaming chunk delivery (stalling), estimated ~8% of active streams affected. Paging on-call SRE. @oncall-bot please escalate to on-call. :phone:

oncall-bot: @tom (oncall) paged at 22:15 UTC — acknowledgement required.

tom: I have it. joining. Observing canary: proxy write queue length for canary nodes dropping ~40% after config change, p99 trending down to ~2.1s.

rene: good. Any errors in application workers after toggles? Nothing alarming in worker logs. Slight increase in 499 / aborted by client.

zara: customer-facing mitigation: setting transparent retry on client SDKs? Not ideal. Instead we should keep customers informed: posting on status as partial degradations for streaming endpoints.

maya: will keep canary for 10min and then expand to 50% if stable. If p99 continues to drop and write queue normalizes, plan full rollout. If aborted connections increase >3% of streams, rollback.

tom: live note: expanding to 50% at 22:23 UTC. Watching metrics.

ops-bot: alert: expansion successful, no immediate regressions. p99 now ~1.6s, p95 ~320ms, proxy queue normalized.

leo: reminder: follow-up action items post-incident: - audit client backpressure patterns (SSE vs WS), - add per-route backpressure metrics, - consider adaptive chunk buffering in proxy.

maya: creating issue with triage notes and attaching flame graphs + sample trace. Will include mitigation commands and rollback window.

tom: handing off to overnight on-call @leo at 23:00 UTC — leave note in incident doc, set paging thresholds lower for next 24h.

oncall-bot: Hand-off complete. Incident mitigated for now; monitoring continues.

zara: final customer impact note: transient stalls affecting ~8% active streams, no data loss, some clients had to reconnect. Recommend status update and postmortem.

maya: agreed. Postmortem template: timeline, root-cause hypothesis (client slow consumers + insufficient proxy eviction), mitigation steps taken, permanent fixes, and SLA impact calc.

ops-bot: Incident closed to active response at 23:10 UTC. Marking as "mitigated — monitoring". Please file postmortem and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
